projections.text: Jamie reports establishing @NYCArtC as a shared coalition publishing identity and connecting it across the coalition, Let NYC Dance, Talks Not Raids, Save NYC Spaces, and FairRentNYC. Public profiles corroborate those connections, not the account-creation history. Teammates also published through the account, so individual posts are not attributed to Jamie without separate evidence.

supports: explicit relationship to four campaign hashtags

boundaries: The public sites and profile establish a shared identity system; Jamie's account-establishment role is first-person evidence.
Do not attribute every coalition post to Jamie or erase Olympia Kazi and other collaborators' stewardship.
A long-lived account does not by itself establish campaign outcomes or audience impact.

projections.text: Jamie reports establishing that shared address, giving collaborators a durable public identity that Council-member accounts could recognize, reply to, invite, and amplify across campaigns. Public profiles corroborate the identity system, not its creation history. A bounded 2026 review recovered 20 returned posts from accounts of seven then-sitting Council members. This is account-level evidence, not formal endorsement or proof of personal authorship.

supports: temporal separation of three out-of-term posts
conservative exclusion of one near-duplicate same-event invitation

projections.text: Jamie reports establishing KC Town Hall's public account as part of the project's identity system; the surviving profile corroborates the account-to-project relationship, not its creation history. Its timeline later functioned as a resident-facing operations channel for neighborhood information and recurring #TiredOfTires pickups; account authorship and program stewardship are not assigned to Jamie post by post.

supports: resident-facing neighborhood information and city-account interaction

boundaries: The account-establishment role is Jamie's first-person account; the public timeline independently establishes the account's later function.
Do not attribute every post, every pickup, or later program stewardship to Jamie.
Keep the public account timeline separate from the CCED funding lifecycle and the later stewardship transition.

projections.text: Jamie designed a shared intake path, recurring meetings, reusable messages, a process for gathering stories with permission, and an implementation plan for a Commercial Rent Stabilization collaboration. He also created an initial shared working record: running minutes, open questions, action items, privacy rules, and named next steps that gave collaborators a place to track follow-up and carry decisions forward. Campaign decisions and outcomes remained collective.

Created an initial shared record for meetings, open questions, action items, privacy rules, and named next steps, while designing broader coordination tools for a Commercial Rent Stabilization collaboration. Campaign decisions and outcomes remained collective.

boundaries: Keep current coalition records private.

projections.text: Jamie describes his role as helping to establish and produce the coalition's recurring participation system: public event pages, meetings rotated among cultural spaces, practical safety and advocacy sessions, and pathways from artist concerns to public hearings and campaign action. Public event records corroborate the system and Jamie's documented participation, while the complete production-responsibility map remains under research.

Twelve recovered recurring-meeting records span ten distinct named physical venues and two virtual meetings; the wider event population also includes public hearings, rallies, training and Q&A sessions, venue-support actions, and relief coordination.

supports: the recurring meeting format and its mix of safety, listening, survey, and town-hall work
the rotating cultural-space practice and policy-to-action format
a cultural-space town hall connecting lived concerns with public officials
independent reporting on the town hall, its approximate attendance, and city-participant context
Jamie's named coalition advocacy and the coalition's practical fire-safety study groups

boundaries: Credit the event practice and outcomes collectively; Jamie's first-person account supports his contribution, not sole organization or authorship.
Do not attribute every event page, invitation, or facilitation decision to Jamie without event-level production evidence or collaborator confirmation.
The event record supports a recurring rotating-venue practice, not an uninterrupted monthly schedule in every year.
Policy outcomes require independent official evidence and collective-work language.
